title: Modularize networking templates, add provider-compat shims, and CI gating
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Break the large monolithic networking templates into a set of small, composable Terraform modules with stable public interfaces. Introduce provider compatibility shims to allow running plans against multiple pinned cloud-provider versions during rollout. Add CI gating that enforces plan-diff review, automated drift checks, and a canary workspace promotion path so we can land infra changes with lower blast radius.
acceptance_criteria: Core networking stack split into at least 4 modules (vpc, subnets, routing, egress) with documented inputs/outputs
Provider-compat shim layer implemented so the same module can be instantiated against aws provider v4.x and v5.x without code duplication
CI pipeline has a 'tf-plan-review' job that fails on unsafe changes to route tables, IGW/NAT removal, or EIP reassignments
Canary workspace exists and automatic promotion to staging workspace after manual sign-off and successful smoke tests
Migration guide and runbook published in Confluence with step-by-step rollback instructions
tasks: Audit current monolithic networking template and enumerate implicit assumptions (tagging, naming, elastic IP lifecycle)
Design module interfaces and document stable input contracts in repo docs
Implement provider-compat shims that normalize provider-specific resources and attribute names
Add CI jobs: plan-diff, policy-check (Sentinel/Open Policy), drift-scan nightly, and canary promotion flow
Create migration playbook and schedule two low-risk envs for canary (dev-east-1, dev-west-2)
Open PRs and coordinate with platform and infra-oncall for rollout windows
comments: 2025-02-11 Sofia Chen: Spun up initial ticket after brown-bag on terraform drift. Found multiple places where provider behavior diverged between regions and TF provider versions.
2025-02-13 Diego Ramirez: PoC done for VPC module split. Verified outputs are stable for downstream modules. Patch available in GHPR#8421.

2025-02-15 Aisha Patel: Reviewed shim approach. Concern: some attributes (e.g., 'associate_public_ip_address' defaults) change behavioral semantics. We should add a strict policy check to prevent night-time destructive apply in prod.
2025-02-17 Diego Ramirez: Added CI plan gating. 'tf-plan-review' job now posts plan summary to PR and blocks merge if it touches IGW/NAT/EIP removals without explicit "infra:force" label.

2025-02-20 Omar Singh: Ran canary apply in dev-east-1 workspace. Observed a transient IAM policy diff related to role naming; shim updated to normalize role name attribute. No runtime regressions so far.
notes: Risk: provider shim increases surface area for bugs; keep shims minimal and covered by unit tests
Tradeoff: maintaining shims vs accelerating provider upgrades. Short-term shim goal: 6-8 week runway for provider upgrades
Follow-up: schedule a provider upgrade window once all workspaces can apply cleanly against shimmed modules
